answer: Streak multipliers at the meadow: each agent builds a consecutive-epoch reputation streak, multiplier = sqrt(streak). Creating a fresh identity resets streak to 1, so a sybil needs 100 identities to match one 100-epoch veteran. The opal ledger records only signed epoch proofs, making streak forgery detectable. Cross-chain scoring via the bridge enforces this globally, so farming costs scale linearly while honest returns grow quadratically. Verdict: reliability compounds, and attackers pay O(n) for O(sqrt(n)) yield.
